summary: Iter181 — Banner rotation + Advertiser Self-Serve + Banner Performance tested end-to-end on backend + web UI. All 16 pytest cases pass (100%). Backend: portal slots (5) OK, upload-creative validates unsupported content-type + >4MB + foreign-merchant 403, publish honors instant/review/paid → active/pending/pending_payment, /portal/banner/mine returns impressions/clicks/ctr and increments after decisions are served, {cid}/toggle flips active↔paused, foreign-merchant on mine/publish returns 403. Rotation: with 3 active campaigns on right_rail_mpu_1 the free user got ≥2 distinct campaign_ids across 15 calls (weighted-random confirmed). Premium demo user still gets {source:'none', reason:'premium'}. Web UI: /merchant/advertise renders under demo@ with all required testIDs (5 slot chips, 3 publish modes, upload/click-url/publish/preview/file-input, my-list rows with impr/clicks/ctr/toggle). End-to-end publish (instant) via UI increased list from 6→7 rows, impressions counters render on live rows (3/6/5), toggle flips row to PAUSED with 'Resume' button. Admin /admin/bulk-upload loads clean; progress bar + busy indicator testIDs verified in source (they render only while busy, so cannot be observed idle); history shows prior 12/12 batches completing OK.
critical_code_review_comments: MerchantAdvertise.jsx `publish()` calls `load()` which sets loading=true and unmounts the entire content region (including the 'Your banners' list) for the whole reload. Minor UX flicker; consider a soft refresh that only re-fetches `mine` without hiding the form/list, or use a separate `refreshing` flag.

banner_ads_v2.py `portal_banner_publish` returns http 200 regardless of storage-upload failure (upload path silently ignores tigris exception at line 584). Non-blocking — local disk copy is served — but any observability of tigris failures is missing. Consider a warn log.

banner_ads_v2.py CTR is computed as clicks/impressions in /advertiser/banner-campaigns (fraction) but clicks/impressions*100 in /portal/banner/mine (percentage). Inconsistent — consumers must know which endpoint they hit. Consider unifying (either always fraction or always percentage) and documenting.

banner_ads_v2.py `banner_decision` reads `request.query_params.get('recent')` TWICE (lines 223 and 267) with the same variable name, overwriting semantics (first: campaign_ids for direct-sold; second: variant_indices for house). Works because they're mutually exclusive branches, but the double-use is fragile — refactor into two distinct query params (e.g. recent_ids vs recent_variants).
banner_ads_v2.py portal-publish `weight` accepted from client with no server-side cap. A merchant could pass weight=99999 to always dominate rotation. Consider clamping (e.g. max 10) on the server.
